text:
support_jamie: FYI customer (acct: acme-ml) reporting Dedicated placements failing in na-midwest since ~09:10 UTC, getting 429/503s and massive tail latency. Escalating to incidents.

oncall_ryan: tagging. any immediate impact on SLA?

support_jamie: customer says several long-running queues are stuck, they see repeated placement retries + fallback to na-east which then hits auth failures for their private VPC keys.

infra_anya: looking at placement logs now, seeing placement_rejects due to 'gpu_pool_stockout' and 'az_shard_limit' in na-midwest-az2.

sres_maria: can you paste the exact errors?

infra_anya: logs: ```
placement: denied
reason: GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTED
pool: dedicated-na-midwest
tenant: acme-ml
retry_count: 5
```

infra_anya: also seeing autoscaler not launching new nodes because per-az instance quota hit: "quota: launch_instances -> FAILED (instance-limit-exceeded)"

eng_runtime_lee: noisy neighbour? any eviction signals or CUDA OOM?

infra_anya: eviction churn yes, eviction_reason: "preemptible_reclaim" and several noisy_tenant spikes on one host (tenant: video-enc-ops). CPU/GPU saturation metrics attached to thread (summaries below).

support_jamie: customer also reporting that when fallback to na-east happens they get 401s for private key retrieval: "kms access denied" — billing team seemingly blocked the key rotation?

billing_bot: alert: account acme-ml has an invoice dispute flag set at 09:05 UTC, service access limited for some KMS ops.

product_kate: this is ugly because fallback behavior should not rely on KMS calls that can be rate-limited by billing flags. we need short-term mitigation.

oncall_ryan: quick repro steps requested by Eng: 1) Submit reserve placement for acme-ml; 2) Force capacity starvation by saturating pool with low-prio jobs; 3) Observe placement rejection + fallback. can someone simulate?

eng_runtime_lee: I'll repro on staging with identical config. sharing quick command: ```
# simulate noisy tenant
for i in {1..50}; do rdl job submit --pool dedicated-na-midwest --image noisy-encoder --gpu 1 &
done
```

eng_runtime_lee: staging shows same placement rejects when pool is saturated and autoscaler unable to add due to az quota. fallback routing picks na-east where KMS deny causes 401; that's consistent.

infra_anya: immediate mitigations: 1) increase reserve-pool headroom (bump reserved slots + move low-prio to preemptible), 2) request quota bump for na-midwest-az2, 3) temporarily block noisy-tenant video-enc-ops from that pool.

sres_maria: operations checklist: drain noisy host, apply tenant isolate tag, roll back any recent scheduling config, and open cloud quota ticket.

support_jamie: customer asks about billing/auth impacts — can billing lift KMS flag so fallback works?

billing_bot: flagged invoice under review. billing oncall @finance_ops is paged. ETA ~30-45m.

product_kate: medium-term: change fallback to use cached keys and prefer regional model variants instead of cross-region KMS calls. add a circuit breaker so 401s don't cascade into ticket storms.

oncall_ryan: temporary customer-facing note prepared: "We're investigating capacity constraints in na-midwest. We're isolating noisy tenants and requesting quota increases. If you see auth failures during failover, please hold — billing is reviewing an invoice flag which may affect KMS access."

customer_ops: customer has asked for timeline and is threatening to route traffic off-platform if this persists. please prioritize.

eng_runtime_lee: current status: noisy host drained, 5 preemptible jobs evicted, reserved pool increased by 10 slots, autoscaler retrying. placements for acme-ml are being retried now.

infra_anya: opened cloud support ticket #CS-987654 for instance quota bump, and internal ticket INT-2026 to block noisy tenant.

support_jamie: final ask for follow-up: once placement stabilizes confirm no billing KMS blocks remain and perform a post-mortem. I'll hold customer update until we have placements green. :thumbsup:

deploy_bot: deploy notice: autoscale-policy change rolled (reserved_pool +10) by infra_anya @ 09:34 UTC.

oncall_ryan: will monitor for 1 hour then escalate to execs if not resolved. thanks all. :eyes:
